To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
monoclonal antibodies against NeuAc alpha2-6neotetraosyllactosylceramide (NeuAc alpha 2,6Gal beta1,4Glc beta1, 4Gal beta1, 1Cer) detect carcinoma-associated ganglio-series glycolipids.

monoclonal antibodies raised by immunization with the oncofetal ganglioside 6'LMl (IV6NeUAc-nLc4Cer) recognize a family of gangliosides that are enriched in carcinomas, and that these ganglioside are characterized by a terminal sialic acid linked to Gal through an alpha 2- 6 bond.

we have produced a panel of monoclonal antibodies that recognize gangliosides carrying an alpha 2- 6 sialic acid residue and that these antibodies recognize antigens present on a wide variety of carcinomas, but not in normal tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of a new class of gangliosides, with a terminal Neuac alpha 2- 6Gal substitution, that are characteristic of fetal tissues and are expressed in a variety of carcinomas, including colorectal and lung carcinomas.
the identification of gangliosides as tumor antigens.
the development of new reagents, the monoclonal antibodies, which are able to detect the NeuAc alpha 1-6Gal substitution in gangliosides and which may be used for diagnostic purposes in human cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

these antibodies are not specific for a particular tumor, but that they react with an antigen which is expressed on a variety of tumors, including carcinomas of the breast and lung, and colorectal carcinomas.

the antibodies described in this report are specific for NeuAc alpha 6Gal beta 4GlcNAc beta 3Gal beta 4Gluc ceramide and that the NeuAc alpha 4Gal beta 3GalNAc beta 4Glu ceramide is not recognized by the monoclonal antibodies.
these monoclonal antibodies are useful for the diagnosis of carcinoma, and that the NeuAc alpha 6Gal epitope is a potential target for cancer therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the monoclonal antibodies raised in our laboratory against 6'LM 1 recognize gangliosides which are minor components of normal tissues but are highly enriched in many carcinomas, particularly in lung carcinomas and colorectal carcinomas.
the expression of NeuAc alpha 6Gal in gangliosides is associated with carcinomas, but not with normal tissues.

we have obtained monoclonal antibodies which are useful tools for the diagnosis of colorectal carcinoma, and which might be used as probes to investigate the mechanism of expression of the NeuAc alpha 6-6Gal substitution in carcinomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of gangliosides containing NeuAc alpha 1-6Gal is a common feature of carcinomas of different tissues.
the expression of these ganglioside antigens in colorectal carcinomas is not related to a specific histological type of tumor or to a specific stage of the tumor.
the presence of NeuAc alpha 6Gal on glycolipids and glycoproteins is a common feature of human carcinomas.
